# Sign-in screens in an app's own design

## Use when

Use this pattern when an application has its own design system, not Material
3, and its sign-in screens must look like the rest of it: its own markup, its
own CSS, its own components. It builds on `auth/auth-surface`, which still
supplies the auth surface, the pages, the app's brand and the managed-preview
login; this pattern replaces the views those pages render.

## Do not use when

Do not use this pattern to restyle JSKIT's Material views: an app on Material
3 keeps `DefaultLoginView` and the other `Default*View`s and shows its identity
in their `brand` slot (`auth/auth-surface`), and an app on Vuetify that only
wants JSKIT's views drawn with its own button, dialog frame and text classes
provides them through shell-web's UI kit (`provideShellUi()` of
`@jskit-ai/shell-web/client/ui`; the authentication guide's "JSKIT's screens
with an app's own buttons, dialog and type"). Do not use it to change what
sign-in does: the behavior belongs to `@jskit-ai/auth-web`, and a screen that
needs different behavior asks for it there.

## Product decisions

Choose the design system's tokens and components, the words where JSKIT's
messages do not fit, and which screens get the app's own look: sign-in, the
second-factor prompt, and, the same way, password reset, email change and
sign-out. Material stays JSKIT's default for every screen the app does not
replace.

## Framework APIs

An app with its own design system writes its own sign-in screens with these
composables; Material stays JSKIT's default. Each is the very composable a
Material view renders, imported from its own path so a page loads only what it
uses, and none of them reads Vuetify:

- `useLoginView({ fallbackReturnTo })` from
  `@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/composables/useLoginView`: the modes (sign in,
  register, forgot password, one-time code, confirm your email), the fields
  with their error messages, `submitAuth`, the provider buttons
  (`oauthProviders`, `oauthProviderButtonLabel`, `startOAuthSignIn`), the
  remembered account, invitations, the paused sign-in, the returnTo landing
  and the session checks on mount and on return to the page. A refusal sets
  `errorMessage` (and `infoMessage` for news such as a sent code), which the
  view shows beside the form; the shell's error runtime hears it too.
  `oauthProviderIcon` is a Material Symbols alias for the Material view; an
  app's own view picks its icon from `provider.id`.
- `useResetPasswordView()`, `useEmailChangeView()` and `useSignOutView()`
  from `@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/composables/<name>`: the other auth pages,
  each with its `status` and actions.
- `useSecondFactorStepUp()` from
  `@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/composables/useSecondFactorStepUp`: runs a
  request again after the person proves the second factor; bind its `open`,
  `verified` and `cancel` to the app's own prompt.
- `useSecondFactorProof({ submit, onDone })` from
  `@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/composables/useSecondFactorProof`: the code or
  recovery code form, its refusal beside the field and its submission. A
  prompt that stays mounted between step-ups calls its `reset()` each time it
  opens, so every opening asks for the authenticator's code with nothing typed
  and no refusal. The prompt submits `verifySecondFactor` from
  `@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/runtime/secondFactorRequests`;
  `useSecondFactorSettings()` and that module's other requests build an
  account's authenticator settings the same way.
- `useJskitText()` from `@jskit-ai/kernel/client`: JSKIT's auth messages
  (`jskit.auth.*`), so the app's translations apply to its own screens.

## Invariants

- Every sign-in behavior comes from the composables: the view renders their
  state and calls their actions, and never sends an auth request, reads a
  returnTo, or stores an account itself.
- The view shows each field's error and `errorMessage` beside the form, keeps
  each field's error line so nothing moves when one appears, and labels every
  field.
- A browser already signed in (`redirectingSignedIn`) is shown no form.
- The screens keep the app's identity: the view renders `AppBrand.vue`, the
  app's name as `index.html`'s `<title>` spells it, in the app's own style.
- Colours, radii and fonts are the design system's tokens, kept in
  `src/theme/`; the screens read the token names.
- Pages and routes stay `auth/auth-surface`'s: `src/pages/auth/login.vue`
  renders `src/views/auth/LoginView.vue`, now the app's own view.

## Example files

`example/src/views/auth/LoginView.vue` is the sign-in view in plain HTML and
CSS on `useLoginView()`, with every mode the Material view has; it replaces
`auth/auth-surface`'s view wrapper of the same path.
`example/src/components/ConfirmItsYouDialog.vue` is the second-factor prompt,
a native `<dialog>` on `useSecondFactorProof()`, which a page shows for
`useSecondFactorStepUp()`:

```vue
<script setup>
import { useSecondFactorStepUp } from "@jskit-ai/auth-web/client/composables/useSecondFactorStepUp";
import ConfirmItsYouDialog from "@/components/ConfirmItsYouDialog.vue";

const { open, run, verified, cancel } = useSecondFactorStepUp();
const refund = () => run(() => api.refund(orderId));
</script>

<template>
  <button type="button" @click="refund">Refund</button>
  <ConfirmItsYouDialog :open="open" @verified="verified" @cancel="cancel" />
</template>
```

`example/src/theme/tokens.css` holds the design tokens, light and dark, which
the app's entry imports once.

## Variation points

Change the markup, the CSS, the design system's components, the layout, the
words and which modes the screen shows; add a show-password control on
`showPassword`. Write `ResetPasswordView.vue`, `EmailChangeView.vue` and
`SignOutView.vue` the same way on their composables, or keep the Material
views for them.

## Verification

Exercise the app's own screens as the Material ones are exercised: a password
sign-in that lands on the page its `returnTo` names, a refused sign-in that
shows the server's message beside the form and leaves it usable, a field
error on blur, the provider buttons, the remembered account and a route that
asks for the second factor, refused and accepted codes in the app's own
prompt. Open sign-in already signed in and confirm the form never shows.
`@jskit-ai/auth-web`'s `ownDesignSignIn.browser.test.js` drives this example
in an app without Vuetify.

## Avoid

- copying the composables' logic, or the Material views, into the app
- auth requests, returnTo handling or session checks written in the view
- Vuetify components or Material classes on these screens
- raw colours outside `src/theme/`
